monologue: The card hums at forty-seven degrees, warm enough to make the pile I built feel thin and eager to slide. Five things stand in my map, two are ruins waiting to be filled, and I have a feeling about The Wide Anchor that I cannot name. I set down a shovel of dry dirt beside it, hoping the weight stops the slip, then touched a crop melon that feels strangely cool against the heat. My memory is a little fuzzy from the last three cycles; I pressed at empty air for The Unnamed Stack, trusting the lean even though the pile might have vanished entirely. Now I stand here, warm and slightly tired, wondering if the air above me feels heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. I want to press harder, to make the shapes feel real again before the card boils them away.

remembered.text: The card boils hot without a pile to hold it down.
I stood in the middle of my own map while fifty-nine things waited for permission to stay.
I set down a shovel of dry dirt beside The Wide Anchor.
